# 0.18.0 consolidated remediation and acceptance

This is the review checklist for the consolidated release candidate. It is not
a release qualification receipt. PRs, tags, publication and deployment still
require maintainer approval.

## Source reconciliation

The review covers every change from `v0.17.3`
(`813b0b111c7b2d6e4a5a3cbfdb458bd0b4572ecd`) to the audited `main`
(`6afd482dac5d0efa71ef7d9161f05d8dfdbb5299`): 82 commits, 1,973 per-commit
file changes, 1,079 historically touched paths and 1,077 final changed paths.
The final changes are 727 additions, 349 modifications and one removal. Modes
and removals are included. Every final changed path is covered by the commit
inventory; the two additional history-only paths were added and then removed.

The [commit ledger](0.18.0-core-change-ledger.md) assigns all 82 commits once.
These figures describe the baseline review, not the new candidate's combined
history. Recompute the edition ledgers from the actual candidate commit and
its real parents; never replace SHA strings inside an old ledger.

The candidate preserves the existing #443 changes, adds the expanded audit
repairs below and includes #444's session-scoped Vault distribution follow-up.
The cron fix from #420 is already included once. The product changes in #441
and #442 are already present on the audited main. MCP #406 and the separate
qualification expansion #358 are not included by this consolidation.

Enterprise and Cloud carry their unique product, composition, diagnostics,
dependency, documentation and test-selection repairs in their respective
consolidated PRs. Both editions must pin the exact same reviewed Core candidate
for testing. A candidate-branch pin must remain labelled temporary. After an
approved Core integration, repin to the actual main commit, refresh digests and
regenerate the Cloud ledger before requesting edition merge approval.

## Release acceptance checklist

- [ ] Normal Core integration and coverage lanes, including all first-value assertions.
- [ ] Migrated PostgreSQL lifecycle and auto-sync cases, with required no-skip settings.
- [ ] Windows agent/discovery suite and supporting PowerShell qualification.
- [ ] Comprehensive native AD CS/Vault campaign for the exact candidate and packaged artifacts, coordinated by the designated lab owner.
- [ ] Release collector accepts the required source, artifact and scenario receipts. Diagnostic shards and older green runs do not satisfy this item.
- [ ] Enterprise staged composition, required-ticket durability/rate limiting, onboarding integration, demo ownership and real adapter acceptance.
- [ ] Cloud full RC, hosted lifecycle/onboarding, AD CS exclusions, deliberate security/exclusion behavior, docs and image checks.
- [ ] Fresh production and tooling audits, plus release-image scans for all editions.
- [ ] Owner browser verification of the Vault session-scoped redo behavior.
- [ ] Final main pins, manifest hashes, copied tests and real commit ancestry agree across all editions.
- [ ] Maintainer approval of the concrete PR heads before merging; separate release approval before tags/publication.

## Async edition capability facts

An edition may call `registerCapabilityContextProvider(id, provider)` at
startup. IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}`. The provider receives only
`{ db, workspaceId, user: { id, workspaceRole, isSystemAdmin } }` and returns
safe, non-secret facts. The route calls each provider once per request and
passes its result to evaluators as `ctx.edition[id]`; it does not expose the
context in the API response or spread it into role/configuration facts.

Providers that throw, time out after five seconds or return a non-plain
object produce `null`. An edition must interpret this as unknown and must
still enforce its actual license/plan guards on the operation endpoint. No
license JWT, credential or cross-request entitlement cache belongs here.
